title: Metrizable descent and finite-field components of continuous scalar cocycles
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended nonarchimedean norm topology [def-weil-algebraic-closure], [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], and a finite intermediate field $E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $S$ be a profinite space (compact Hausdorff with a clopen basis), $K$ a profinite group (compact Hausdorff with an open normal subgroup basis), and $n\geq1$. All spaces use [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $C^r(P,G;V)=C(P\times G^r,V)$ for all continuous maps, with trivial group action, $d^0=0$, and for $r\geq1$
$$(dc)(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{r+1})=c(s;g_2,\ldots,g_{r+1})+\sum_{a=1}^r(-1)^a c(s;g_1,\ldots,g_ag_{a+1},\ldots,g_{r+1})+(-1)^{r+1}c(s;g_1,\ldots,g_r).$$
For every cocycle $z\in C^n(S,K;\Omega)$ there are a metrizable profinite space $S_0$, a metrizable profinite group $G$, continuous surjections $p:S\to S_0$ and $q:K\to G$ with $q$ a homomorphism, and a cocycle $z_0\in C^n(S_0,G;\Omega)$ with $z=z_0\circ(p\times q^n)$. Every finite continuous quotient of $G$ is a finite continuous quotient of $K$.
There are increasing closed intermediate fields $E\subseteq F_i\subseteq\Omega$ finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with $\bigcup_{i\geq0}F_i=\Omega$, and $F_i$-linear continuous maps $p_i:\Omega\to F_i$ fixing $F_i$ and satisfying $|p_i(x)|\leq |x|$. Set $p_{-1}=0$. The maps
$$e_i=(p_i-p_{i-1})\circ z_0\quad(i\geq0)$$
are continuous $F_i$-valued cocycles; at every fixed $(s,y)\in S_0\times G^n$ they are zero for all sufficiently large $i$. Moreover $p_i\circ z_0\to z_0$ uniformly, $\|e_i\|_\infty\to0$, and $\sum_{i=0}^N e_i=p_N\circ z_0$. The $p_i$ are not required to commute. Empty $S$ is allowed.

source.place: Paragraph (3) is motivation only; agent-formulated analytic lemma extracted from old proof steps 4–5: metrizable quotient descent and pointwise finite, uniformly small scalar components. WANTED: exact norm-topological reference.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-metric-function-quotients] to $z$, $r=n\geq1$, and the metric space $\Omega$ with $d(x,y)=|x-y|$. Its profiniteness hypotheses are exactly ours, and it does not require completeness of the target. Obtain $S_0,G,p,q,z_0$ and $z=z_0\circ(p\times q^n)$, with all the asserted continuity, metrizability and surjectivity properties, including empty $S$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion: metrizable factorization

proof.text: For $(s_0;g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})$, choose $s\in S$ and $k_a\in K$ lifting its coordinates. Since $q(k_ak_{a+1})=g_ag_{a+1}$, substitution in every displayed term of the differential gives $(dz_0)(s_0;g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=(dz)(s;k_1,\ldots,k_{n+1})=0$. This also proves the assertion when $n=1$; empty parameter spaces give no points to check. If $h:G\twoheadrightarrow H$ is any finite continuous quotient homomorphism, $h\circ q:K\twoheadrightarrow H$ is continuous, a homomorphism and surjective. Thus every finite continuous quotient of $G$ is one of $K$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion: cocycle descent and finite quotients

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-algcl-countable-closed-finite-cover] with the given $\ell,\Omega,E$ to obtain increasing closed finite intermediate fields $F_i\supseteq E$ exhausting $\Omega$. For each $i$, apply [lem-sfb-norm-one-finite-subfield-projection] with $F=F_i$ and the same absolute value. Choose its continuous $F_i$-linear contraction $p_i:\Omega\to F_i$, fixing $F_i$, and put $p_{-1}=0$. Both input statements allow the incomplete field $\Omega$; no completion or compatibility between the chosen maps is imposed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion: exhaustion and norm-one projections

proof.text: For $i\geq1$, regard $p_{i-1}$ as a map to $F_i$ by the inclusion $F_{i-1}\subseteq F_i$, which is isometric for the restricted absolute values. The differences $p_i-p_{i-1}:\Omega\to F_i$ are continuous and additive, as is $p_0$. Applying any such additive map to the finite alternating sum defining $d$ commutes with every summand and its sign. Consequently $d e_i=(p_i-p_{i-1})(dz_0)=0$, and $e_i$ is a continuous $F_i$-valued cocycle. For a fixed input $t$, exhaustion gives $z_0(t)\in F_j$ for some $j$; for $i\geq j+1$, both maps fix this value, so $e_i(t)=0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion: finite-field components and pointwise eventual vanishing

proof.text: The domain D = S₀ × Gⁿ is compact by Pi.compactSpace and compactness of products [lem-weil-pbc-tychonoff-product-quasi-compact]. For ε > 0, the open sets Uₐ = {t : ‖z₀(t) − z₀(a)‖ < ε/3} cover D. IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover chooses finitely many centres, including when D is empty. Exhaustion, monotonicity and the fixing property imply that each scalar is eventually fixed by Pᵢ, the composite Ω → Fᵢ → Ω. Thus eventually all those finitely many centre values are fixed simultaneously. For t in Uₐ, Pᵢ(z₀(t)) − z₀(t) = Pᵢ(z₀(t) − z₀(a)) − (z₀(t) − z₀(a)). The ordinary triangle inequality and contractivity bound its norm by 2‖z₀(t) − z₀(a)‖ < 2ε/3 < ε. Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff gives uniform convergence. No nonemptiness or completeness is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion: compact finite-cover uniform estimate

proof.text: Define cᵢ : C(D, Ω) by cᵢ(t) = Pᵢ(z₀(t)). By ContinuousMap.tendsto_iff_tendstoUniformly, uniform convergence gives cᵢ → z₀ in the compact-open (sup-norm) topology. Since i − 1 → ∞, cᵢ − cᵢ₋₁ → 0, and continuity of the norm gives ‖cᵢ − cᵢ₋₁‖ → 0. For i ≠ 0, ContinuousMap.norm_eq_iSup_norm and the restricted norm on Fᵢ identify this norm with ‖eᵢ‖, proving the required norm limit. For each fixed t, both Pᵢ and Pᵢ₋₁ eventually fix z₀(t), so eᵢ(t) = 0 eventually. Induction on N, Finset.sum_range_succ and cancellation give ∑ᵢ₌₀ᴺ eᵢ(t) = P_N(z₀(t)). Only contractivity and the individual fixing properties are used, with no commutativity hypothesis.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion: telescoping and vanishing component norms

proof_origin.place: Paragraph (3) is motivation only. P4 implements the stated factorization, field-exhaustion and projection route. The finite-cover estimate uses radius ε/3 and the ordinary triangle inequality. Sup-norm convergence is obtained from the compact-open topology on continuous maps and convergence of consecutive differences.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q132-047282152 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Six steps, no new nodes. Statement, stmt_deps, source, created and blueprint are identical to the live unsplit node (field diff); there is no repair note for this item. Step 1: the metric-function-quotients statement gives exactly S_0, G, p, q (homomorphism) and continuous z_0, with an arbitrary metric target and empty S allowed. Step 2: lifting through the surjections gives dz_0=0; h∘q settles the finite-quotient clause. Step 3: the countable closed finite cover and the norm-one projection for each F_i match the item's clauses verbatim; no commutation of the p_i is used. Step 4: p_i-p_{i-1}:Ω→F_i is additive and continuous, so d e_i=0; for i≥j+1 both maps fix z_0(t)∈F_j. Step 5: Tychonoff plus a finite ε/2 cover, centres in F_J, and |p_i(w)-w|≤|w|<ε/2 by the ultrametric inequality; I checked this. Step 6: telescoping and the max-of-two-errors bound. Edge cases tested: empty S, n=1, trivial K, E=Q_ℓ, compact image not in one field. Duplicate search: lem-sfb-accelerated-finite-field-cochain-differences (Q49) is a different statement (completion B, primitives, no metrizable descent). Sources: blueprint direct-images ¶(3) is motivation only, as the item says; L19 Prop 1.1.9, first bullet, supports the countable exhaustion. tool_uses: Tychonoff, accepted. Batch-5 flag: algcl-countable-closed-finite-cover → padic-rational-algebraic-generator → padic-minpoly-normed-separation → lem-trf-spectral-norm-algebraic-extension.
